 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANISH DAYAL  ORDER % 15.07.2024 1.
Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition is moved on behalf of petitioner for setting aside order dated 2nd May 2024 passed by the ASJ (POCSO) Rohini, framing charges against the petitioner under Section 21 POCSO Act which provides for punishment for failure in reporting a case.
2. The issue arises out of background of a matrimonial dispute between petitioner and her husband.
A complaint was filed on behalf of daughter on This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/07/2024 at 21:06:31 6th June 2021, who was a minor at the time of commission of the alleged crime, where she went along with petitioner (her mother) to the Police Station Maurya Enclave to register an FIR which was subsequently registered as FIR No. 515/2021 under Sections 354/354A/377 IPC and Section 10 POCSO at PS Maurya Enclave.
3. The allegations made by the daughter were that her father had sexually assaulted her on multiple occasions.
Subsequently, a charge sheet was filed on 27th July 2021.

Subsequently, vide the impugned order, charges were framed against the husband/accused under Sections Rupi Babbar vs State Nct Of Delhi on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182352260/
1 354/354A/376(3) IPC and Sections 6/10/12/21 POCSO.

entities.text: Sections Rupi Babbar vs State Nct Of Delhi
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: On the basis of application moved by the father, petitioner was summoned on 22nd March 2023 and thereafter charges were framed, under Section 21 POCSO.

4. Counsel for petitioner assails the order qua the petitioner to the extent that charges under Section 21 POCSO Act could not be made out since charge sheet itself records that the victim-daughter came along with petitioner/mother to report the matter to police.

It is stated that the mother, i.e.
petitioner herself was a victim of abuse and had also been summoned, as a victim, for recording of her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate on 11th June 2021.

5. Counsel for petitioner relies upon the decision of a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Jasvinder Kaur &Anr. v. State &Anr.[2024:DHC:3677] wherein it is held in the facts of the case that Section 21 of the Act provides for punishment for "failure to report" and not delay in reporting.
The trial is expected to commence tomorrow.
6. Issue notice.
7. APP for the State accepts notice.
8. Status report be filed in this regard before the next date of hearing,
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/07/2024 at 21:06:31 along with any other law on which he wishes to rely in this regard.

9. Considering that the nature of the offence are fairly serious and the victim-daughter has since attained majority; in order to state her version, the Investigating Officer shall inform the prosecutrix/complainant in writing regarding the pendency of the present matter to enable her to be present in the Court personally or through authorized representative/counsel, if she so desires.
It is clarified that it is not compulsory for the prosecutrix/complainant to appear in person.

10. List on 30th July 2024.
11. Copy of order be given dasti under the signature of the Court Master.
12. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J JULY 15, 2024/sm
